statements.venue: Letter to Secretary of State Rubio and UN Ambassador Waltz (sole signer)
statements.quote: Even employees from America’s top two AI labs warn that this technology is racing to a finish line for humanity.
statements.context: Barrett cites a Wall Street Journal report on an Anthropic researcher who quit over out-of-control AI fears, then writes in the next paragraph: "I believe we must take these warnings seriously".
statements.reason: A relayed warning that AI threatens humanity, endorsed in his own words ("we must take these warnings seriously"); boundary because the phrase is figurative and he then frames the risk as one to national security.

statements.venue: Letter to Secretary of State Rubio and UN Ambassador Waltz, quoted in press release
statements.quote: This next frontier in emerging technology has the ability to propel this world into a golden age or send us into collapse.
statements.context: Closing of his letter urging international AI talks, including with adversaries, before it is too late.
statements.reason: States in his own words that AI could send the world into collapse, a catastrophic risk not limited to misuse; boundary with C because the harm is not specified.

statements.venue: Letter to Secretary of State Rubio and UN Ambassador Waltz (sole signer)
statements.quote: The dangerous reality is that AI – in the wrong hands – can be used to carry out highly sophisticated cyberattacks on our energy grid, deliver a lethal biological weapon into our communities, or undermine our banking system.
statements.context: Arguing the US must win the AI race so adversaries cannot weaponize AI.
statements.reason: Names biological weapons and grid attacks, but only as misuse by people, so C under the misuse-only ruling.

statements.quote: We are already seeing it replace American jobs, threaten our national security, and degrade human dignity. These risks cannot be ignored
statements.context: Introducing the Artificial Intelligence Governance and Emerging Threats Act to create a Cabinet-level office on AI threats.
statements.reason: The harms named are jobs, a general national security threat and human dignity, which are D under the rulings.

statements.quote: Artificial intelligence is playing an increasingly critical role in strengthening our national defense, but it should never be the one making life-or-death decisions,
statements.context: Introducing a bill with Beyer and Jacobs requiring human oversight of autonomous and AI weapons.
statements.reason: Military use of AI and human control of lethal force is D under ruling 3.

intl.note: His 29 Sep 2026 letter urges talks with allies and adversaries toward an international AI treaty, incident sharing, risk management and human control of nuclear weapons, but does not mention China by name or coordinating on the pace of AI development or a pause, so it does not meet the definition; a reviewer may want to weigh this.
sources: Barrett letter to Rubio and Waltz, 29 Sep 2026

rsi.note: No statement found on a ban on self-improving AI.

record: Sole-signed letter urging Secretary Rubio and Ambassador Waltz to pursue an international AI agreement and treaty, with allies and adversaries
Introduced the Artificial Intelligence Governance and Emerging Threats Act (H.R. 10768) creating a Cabinet-level Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats
Introduced, with Beyer and Jacobs, the Human Authority over Autonomous Weapons Act (H.R. 9729)
Listed as having introduced or co-sponsored the AI Threat Output and Monitoring Incident Containment Act (H.R. 9965), to test advanced AI systems to prevent risks to nuclear safety
grade_reason: In a 2026 letter he relays lab employees' warning that AI is "racing to a finish line for humanity" and says "we must take these warnings seriously", which ruling 2 makes A; he also says in his own words AI could "send us into collapse" (B). No dismissive statement found. The A rests on one figurative, endorsed relayed warning, so B is a defensible alternative.
